transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-04-13 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Jordan Reed (CTO, Pegasus), Aisha Khan (SRE), Liam Myers (PM)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on per-path/per-route usage telemetry, cost attribution, and how Redwood's dashboard can slice by service, model variant, and environment (hosted vs dedicated). Discussed security/KMS/SSO concerns and next steps for a 1-week pilot and bench tests.

Topics:
- Per-path dashboards & cost breakdown
- Tagging and attribution for multi-tenant flows
- Hosted vs Dedicated routing and failover policies
- Security: SOC2, SAML, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- Pilot scope and benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we, um, scheduled 45 but we have 52 today so plenty of time. I'm Ethan, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Maya, our solutions eng. Jordan, thanks for coordinating.
[00:18] Jordan: Yeah thanks Ethan, appreciate it. We booked this because we want to see the console—like, specifically how we can tell which customer routes are burning spend. We've got a lot of opaque token spend right now.
[00:31] Aisha: And also we need to understand the telemetry retention and what we can pull into our internal billing.
[00:39] Maya: Great, we'll start on the console, show the route-level lenses, then dive into cost maps and the tagging system. I'll also show a quick canary rollout example.
[00:48] Liam: Awesome. Also curious about latency breakdown per model variant.

[01:02] Maya: Ok pulling up the dashboard, quick note — this is a sandbox view with synthetic data. Top left you can filter by time range, model family and environment. Here we have a 'per-path' selector — you can map one or many HTTP routes or internal functions to a route.
[01:22] Ethan: (interrupts) One thing to call out, we automatically attribute tokens to routes if you pass route metadata in the header or via the SDK, but you can also do dynamic tag mapping on the console.
[01:36] Jordan: So if I have 200 endpoints, can I do a group-by to roll them up by product area?
[01:44] Maya: Yes, group-by works on any tag — service, product_line, env. We show both raw token counts and normalized cost units. The cost model is customizable — you can bring your own unit cost if you're on Dedicated.
[01:59] Aisha: How accurate is the mapping if requests get proxied and the route header is lost?
[02:07] Maya: Good question. We have fallback attribution using input host and request path heuristics, but it's best practice to carry the route meta. If not, you can ingest logs and do a mapping import.
[02:21] Jordan: Hmm, ok.

[02:40] Maya: Moving to the cost breakdown chart — this is per-route spend over time, with drill-down into per-model and per-instance. You can select a spike and it will show the exact requests that contributed. This is helpful for root-causeing sudden spend increases.
[02:58] Liam: Can you export those request samples? We need them for internal audits.
[03:05] Maya: Yes, CSV export is supported, and there's an API to pull the same data programmatically.

[03:20] Ethan: I want to highlight the route-level SLA view — you can set latency SLOs per route and get alerts. If a route starts breaching, Redwood can auto-route to a cheaper fallback model or to dedicated capacity depending on your policy.
[03:36] Jordan: Wait, auto-route to cheaper fallback — how do you ensure quality doesn't drop?
[03:44] Maya: We support model families and quality tiers. You configure which variants are acceptable as fallbacks and Redwood keeps evals so you can compare outputs on a sample set. The console shows a quality delta estimate when you pick a fallback.
[03:58] Aisha: Is that based on our own evals or Redwood's?
[04:03] Maya: Both — you can upload your evals and prompts or use Redwood-verified benchmarks. For privacy we run the evals in your project, not across tenants.

[04:20] Jordan: Security — we need SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, KMS for key management, and audit logs going to our SIEM. Is all that available?
[04:31] Ethan: Yes on the enterprise plan. SAML and SCIM are supported, audit logs are exportable to your SIEM, and we integrate with AWS KMS and HSMs for private key storage.
[04:44] Liam: Do you have SOC2 Type II? We get that request a lot.
[04:48] Ethan: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO are in our compliance kit. We'll share the security pack.

[05:02] Maya: Back to telemetry — here's the 'cost attribution map' where you can see token cost split by model, route, and customer-id. We also show cache hit rates for KV/prefix caching which impacts per-token cost.
[05:18] Aisha: Our engineers have been talking about KV cache but not sure how Redwood's caching would integrate with our edge.
[05:26] Maya: The runtime exposes a cache API and automatically caches prefixes if you enable it. For private deployments you can have the cache colocated. There's a config to control ttl and eviction. For edge proxies you can propagate cache keys with headers.
[05:42] Jordan: What's the expected savings from caching?
[05:46] Maya: Depends on workload; for high prefix reuse we see 20-60% token cost reduction. For chatty session-based flows caching KV significantly reduces the decode work.

[06:05] Ethan: We also have a 'route economics playbook' — it suggests batching sizes, quantization level, and whether to use Dedicated for heavy routes. It uses historical distribution to recommend configs.
[06:18] Liam: So it's automated recommendations? Could be dangerous if it recommends quantization for a customer-facing summary flow.
[06:27] Maya: The recommended profiles come with a risk score and expected quality impact. You review before applying. And we support staged rollouts — canary first, then fleet.

[06:45] Jordan: Talking about Dedicated — we need predictable throughput for our compliance-critical flows. How do you guarantee that?
[06:53] Ethan: Dedicated capacity gives you reserved GPU pools, you can pin models and get throughput SLOs. We also publish latency percentiles for those pools.
[07:03] Aisha: And private deployments — if we wanted an air-gapped install, is that feasible?
[07:08] Maya: Yes, we have a private package. It runs with a customer-managed control plane, you bring your infra and we provide the runtime and ops tooling. There's a slightly different observability integration but similar dashboards.

[07:25] Jordan: Data residency — we need logs to remain in EU for certain customers.
[07:30] Ethan: You can configure region-level retention and log export endpoints. We'll scope that in the pilot.

[07:44] Liam: Pricing — how do you charge for console and per-route visibility?
[07:50] Ethan: Console and telemetry features are included, pricing is primarily per-token for hosted and blended rates for Dedicated (commitment + usage). We can show a projected cost model for your traffic mix.

[08:05] Maya: Quick demo of drill-in: selecting a spike on Route /checkout-validate, you can see token distribution across prompt vs completion, which model handled the call, and what policies were applied. There's also a timeline of rollout changes.
[08:28] Aisha: The UI labels look a bit generic — can we map to our internal service names?
[08:33] Maya: Yes, you can import a mapping CSV or use the API to push canonical names.

[08:45] Jordan: One of our concerns is telemetry overhead. Will the extra tags and logging add latency?
[08:52] Maya: We try to piggyback tags on existing headers; minimal overhead. For heavy flows we recommend sampling (1-5%) for full request dumps but we still attribute tokens for all requests.

[09:07] Ethan: I'll pause and see if there are deeper technical questions?
[09:12] Aisha: Yes, one thing — where does the KV cache live in Hosted mode?
[09:17] Maya: In hosted, the cache is in the serving layer, distributed across nodes. For Dedicated or Private you can colocate and configure replication.

[09:32] Jordan: If we wanted to run a 1-week pilot with production-like traffic, what's the minimum setup?
[09:38] Ethan: Typically we do a scoped pilot: pick 3-5 representative routes, set up API keys, enable route headers, decide whether to use hosted or dedicated trial nodes, and run 7 days of traffic. Maya will draft a benchmark plan.
[09:53] Liam: Will you let us run canary fallbacks during pilot? We want to see quality deltas live.
[09:58] Maya: Absolutely, canary and A/B rollouts are part of the demo; we can instrument evals for the samples.

[10:10] Jordan: About billing — we need per-product chargebacks. Does the console export a daily invoice with route split?
[10:16] Ethan: You can configure daily or weekly reports, and we have an accounting API endpoint that returns cost-breakdown by route label.

[10:30] Aisha: Security again, we'll need penetration test evidence and a timeline for incident response.
[10:36] Ethan: We'll include our security incident SLA and pen test summary in the pack.

[10:48] Maya: Now a short walkthrough of the 'Optimize' tab — it ingests route history and suggests batching, lower-precision quantization and cheaper model variants for non-critical routes. You can preview estimated monthly savings before applying.
[11:05] Liam: Does Optimize consider multi-tenant fairness? Our routes are shared across tenants.
[11:12] Maya: We have policies for tenant-aware optimizations; you can opt to only apply optimizations at the route scope, not tenant, or the reverse.

[11:28] Jordan: Who typically owns the mapping of routes to business units?
[11:33] Ethan: Usually the product org or infra tags them; Redwood can help with an initial mapping consult as part of the pilot.

[11:45] Maya: Quick note on observability: token-level traces include sampling id, route, model, replica id. You can link to your tracing system using our trace hooks. Some transcriptions in the system might show model names truncated as 'rdw-model-v2', transcription artifacts are common in generated labels.

[12:03] Liam: That brings me to compliance — we need logs retained 7 years for some regulated customers. Is that configurable?
[12:09] Ethan: Yes retention is configurable per dataset with tiered storage. We'll need to discuss archival costs.

[12:22] Jordan: Any known limitations we should watch for?
[12:26] Maya: For extremely high qps short bursty traffic, you might see cold-start latencies; we recommend pre-warming for critical routes. Also some legacy model architectures may not support certain quant paths.

[12:42] Aisha: On the model side, what about kernel selection and GPU SKU differences — will that affect per-token cost?
[12:50] Maya: Yes, GPU SKU affects cost and latency. The console exposes per-node metrics and we show recommended instance types in the Optimize tab.

[13:04] Jordan: Could you show a sample of the benchmark results?
[13:08] Maya: Sure — here's a CSV we generated from a demo run. It's a bit noisy, transcription note: speaker alignment may be off. (link: https://redwood.example/demo/pegasus-bench-04-13.csv)

[13:26] Ethan: Quick pause — any blockers for starting a pilot?
[13:30] Jordan: Security review timeline is the main blocker, and budget sign-off for the pilot reserved nodes if needed.
[13:37] Ethan: We'll aim to get the security pack over by Friday.

[13:45] Maya: For the pilot plan I'll outline the routes, expected QPS, success criteria (cost delta, latency change, quality delta), and the runbook for rollbacks.

[13:58] Liam: Success criteria — can we define a cost cap for the pilot and quality thresholds?
[14:04] Maya: Yes we'll set thresholds: e.g., <5% quality regression on NPS prompts, latency within 95th percentile SLO, and cost per 1k tokens under projected cap.

[14:18] Jordan: Anything else on the console side?
[14:21] Ethan: One more feature — anomaly detection on spend; it flags unusual spend growth by route and can auto-open a ticket in Jira.
[14:31] Aisha: That's useful. We use PagerDuty — does it integrate?
[14:35] Ethan: Yes PagerDuty, Slack, and webhook integrations supported.

[14:47] (long pause while Maya toggles settings)
[15:05] Maya: Last demo item — tagging templates. You can create a template that enforces tags on ingestion so downstream teams get harmonized labels.
[15:16] Liam: We will need that.

[15:22] Jordan: Okay looks good, let's talk timeline. If we get the pack Friday and security review completes within a week, we can aim for the pilot start on April 26th.
[15:33] Ethan: Sounds doable. Next steps recap: I'll send the security/compliance kit, pricing sheet and pilot T&Cs. Maya will deliver the benchmark plan and sample scripts. Jordan will confirm stakeholder list and security contacts.

[15:48] Aisha: One last question — do you have references with similar compliance needs?
[15:52] Ethan: Yes we have two customers in fintech with similar controls; I'll connect you.

[16:00] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[16:03] Ethan: Thank you — we'll follow up with links.

End of call.
